subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw expose append semantics on the existing `write` tool, require a separate append tool, or defer this to a broader file-safety design?
rationale: The source-reproducible data-loss class is clear, but the fix changes a model-facing and extension-observable core tool contract, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept append on write
options.body: Proceed with the linked pull request's backwards-compatible `append: true` shape after resolving conflicts and verifying host, workspace, and sandbox behavior.

options.title: Require a separate append surface
options.body: Keep `write` as explicit overwrite and ask for a replacement that adds a dedicated append tool or `mode` contract with the same safety guards.

options.title: Pause for broader file safety
options.body: Defer the linked implementation until maintainers decide on append, locking, backups, overwrite naming, and protected shared files together.

recommendation.title: Accept append on write
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked pull request's backwards-compatible `append: true` shape after resolving conflicts and verifying host, workspace, and sandbox behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the documented project lead and the strongest current-main history signal for the agent write and memory tool surfaces involved in this API decision.
